other_resources.name: aws_elasticache_parameter_group.kong
other_resources.note: Custom parameter group with no parameters set (all defaults). Its family must change to the target family (valkey9 for the recommendation) in the same change. The name is fixed (format("%s-%s", service, environment)), so a family change forces replacement of a group that is in use; the remediation needs a new name or create-before-destroy.

findings.title: Redis OSS 5.0.5 replication group is in paid Extended Support
findings.description:
aws_elasticache_replication_group.kong (redis.tf:1) uses engine = "redis" (redis.tf:7) with engine_version = var.redis_engine_version, default "5.0.5" (variables.tf:487). Redis OSS 5 left standard support on 2026-01-31 and has been in Extended Support since 2026-02-01 (source: AWS docs, no live data). Next price step 2027-02-01 (Year 2, still 80%), Year 3 from 2028-02-01 (160%), end of Extended Support 2029-01-31, after which AWS upgrades it to the latest Valkey. The declared 5.0.5 was most likely upgraded to 5.0.6 by AWS; unconfirmed. The resource is created only when enable_redis=true (default false), so it may not be deployed. Risk Medium (3): automatic failover / Multi-AZ off (+2), no staging environment found (+1). Recommended: Valkey 9.1 (rule 3). Alternatives: Valkey 8.2, Valkey 7.2 (in-place rollback to Redis OSS 7.1), Redis OSS 7.1. Estimated Extended Support exposure about $40/month (estimate, see pricing page).

findings.title: Parameter group family redis5.0 must change with the engine; fixed name forces replacement
findings.description: aws_elasticache_parameter_group.kong uses family = var.redis_family, default "redis5.0" (variables.tf:494), and sets no custom parameters. Any upgrade target needs a new family (valkey9, valkey8, valkey7 or redis7). Changing family forces replacement, and the name format("%s-%s", var.service, var.environment) is fixed and referenced by the replication group (redis.tf:11), so the old group cannot be deleted while in use. The remediation should give the new group a distinct name or use create_before_destroy, and update parameter_group_name in the same apply.

findings.title: Warning: transit_encryption_enabled is unset (Valkey target, Terraform)
findings.description: In-transit encryption is not set, so it is off. The AWS provider documents it as optional, but whether an in-place Redis to Valkey change is accepted without TLS isn't confirmed in the docs. Turning on TLS changes how Kong connects (it would need redis_ssl=true). Don't enable it automatically: decide, then verify with terraform plan before applying.

findings.title: Warning: at_rest_encryption_enabled is unset (Valkey target, Terraform)
findings.description: The provider default differs by engine (false for redis, true for valkey). Changing engine to valkey with the attribute unset can show an encryption change on the existing cache. Run a real terraform plan before apply; if it shows a change to at_rest_encryption_enabled or transit_encryption_enabled, or any -/+ replacement, stop and set the attribute explicitly to the live value (false).

findings.title: AWS provider version is not constrained; CI pins Terraform 0.12.13
findings.description: The module has no terraform/required_providers block, so the AWS provider version is chosen by the caller and couldn't be resolved. engine = "valkey" on aws_elasticache_replication_group needs a recent 5.x (or later) AWS provider; confirm the minimum in the provider changelog. The CI workflow runs only fmt and init with Terraform 0.12.13 (lines 14 and 21), which is too old for current provider releases. Not reported as a blocker because no constraint exists to bump; callers must confirm their provider version before remediation.

findings.title: Previous-generation node type cache.t2.small: confirm it is offered for the target engine
findings.description: redis_instance_type defaults to cache.t2.small (previous generation). Confirm the node type is supported for the chosen Valkey or Redis OSS 7.1 version in the Region before the upgrade; if not, a node type change (for example to cache.t3.small or cache.t4g.small) is needed as a separate step.
